title: Firm developing Portsmouth site data center posts $7B loss
summary: Japanese investment firm SoftBank Group, whose subsidiary SB Energy is developing what the Department of Energy calls “the world’s largest artificial intelligence data center” at the Portsmouth, Ohio, nuclear cleanup site, has posted a net quarterly loss of approximately $7 billion. The PORTS Technology Campus (also known as the PORTS-Pike Technology Campus), which the Department of Energy’s Office of Environmental Management announced in March, is slated to be home to a 10-GW AI data center developed through a partnership between SB Energy and OpenAI, with Nvidia providing computing infrastructure for the facility. According to the November 10 episode of DOE-EM’s EnergyCast podcast, the campus also will host the largest energy generation project in the United States. SB Energy has pledged to build 10 GW of new power generation at the site to support the data center, including 9.2 GW of power from natural gas–powered turbines.

IAEA publishes 2026 World Fusion Outlook
summary: The fourth edition of the International Atomic Energy Agency’s World Fusion Outlook is now available. The 128-page report is described by the IAEA as an examination of industry developments, including the advancement of fusion power plant concepts into industrial programs, the evolution of experimental fusion machines into integrated facilities, the emergence of a global fusion supply chain, and increased private and governmental investment in fusion energy.

title: Constellation Q3 updates: New Peak+, uprates, restart, midterm elections
summary: Constellation has signed a 270-MW agreement with a customer that would link support for clean energy resources like nuclear to other new power generation resources. This agreement under Constellation's Peak+ program was one of several nuclear-related items highlighted by Constellation executives at its third-quarter earnings call Monday. Other topics mentioned included the recent flurry of uprate announcements, the Crane restart, and the midterm elections.

title: OPG Begins ‘Comprehensive Assessment’ As Canada SMR Project Faces Delays And Budget Overruns
summary: The first of four BWRX-300 small modular reactors (SMRs) under construction at the Darlington nuclear site in Canada will not be on schedule or to budget, Ontario Power Generation (OPG) has said. OPG said in its 2026 third quarter financial results that it had previously noted that the Darlington New Nuclear Project (DNNP) is subject to “inherent risks and uncertainties that could affect project cost and schedule”.

title: Pouring Of First Concrete Begins For Nuclear Island At China’s Sanao-4
summary: First concrete pouring has begun for the nuclear island of Unit 4 at the Sanao nuclear power station in eastern Chinese province of Zhejiang, project owner China General Nuclear (CGN) announced on Tuesday (10 November). The company said the pouring of first concrete began at 08:28 local time on 10 November, marking the official start of main construction. It said the total volume of concrete poured as of 10 November was approximately 8,820 cubic metres and the process is expected to last 60 hours.
